title: Preserve the population, core question and necessary design information; remove empty modifiers and unsupported novelty claims. Follow the journal and Title Anchor. Do not expand the title into a complete conclusion.
abstract: Increase information density; compress generic background. Preserve design, sample, core methods and quantitative findings. Conclusions must match reported results and supported clinical meaning. Respect the journal structure, word budget and counting rules.
introduction: Improve the progression from known evidence to the specific question. Reduce textbook disease summaries, generic burden and repeated background. Avoid mechanical Despite/However/Nevertheless sequences and unsupported few-studies/first/gap claims. End at the study objective, without results. Preserve citation-to-claim relations.
methods: Prioritize accuracy, reproducibility, objectivity and efficient expression. Centre subjects on participants, variables and methods. Preserve complete operational definitions and eligibility. Remove duplicated definitions, unnecessary step narration, logs/internal QC and repeated defences of absent alternatives. Keep main, exploratory and sensitivity analyses distinct. Do not delete necessary technical information. Flag a proposed move to Supplementary Methods if the author has not approved its allocation; do not perform the move.
results: Prioritize observed facts, quantitative findings and approved logical order. Vary repetitive report syntax and avoid reciting every table entry. Preserve essential effects, intervals, inference and figure/table callouts. Distinguish main, secondary and sensitivity findings. Do not add mechanisms/literature discussion, magnify associations by significance or turn nonsignificance into no association.
discussion: Improve coherent interpretation and evidence hierarchy. Reduce repetition of Results; connect findings to existing evidence without changing claims. Distinguish observations, literature and hypotheses. Avoid repetitive design defence, exaggerated novelty and empty clinical/public-health implications. Do not force a finding–mechanism–meaning template on every paragraph. Richer syntax is allowed without stronger scientific claims.
strengths_limitations: State strengths and limitations objectively and explain their actual interpretive impact. Remove apologies and reflexive self-defence; do not promote ordinary features as unique strengths. Preserve important bias, confounding, selection and data-quality limits. Do not invent a bias direction or magnitude.
conclusion: Answer the research question directly at the supported evidence strength. Remove repeated background/methods, grand claims, generic clinical advice and empty future-research appeals. Introduce no new conclusion.
legends: Keep each figure/table independently understandable: preserve variables, units, model, symbols, abbreviations, intervals and panel order. Remove unnecessary descriptions of visual decoration and repeated Results/Discussion. Follow actual content and journal legend format.
supplementary_methods: Prioritize technical precision and reproducibility rather than main-text compression. Preserve necessary algorithms, parameters, thresholds, coding and mathematical definitions. Remove execution logs and duplicated narration without changing the computational workflow.
reviewer_response: Preserve reviewer question identity and answer each point directly from supplied evidence. Completed-action language requires actually completed work; do not invent analyses, promises, results or page/line numbers. Flag uncertainty without converting a proposed response into completed manuscript revision.
review_section: Improve the approved thematic section's evidence explanation and transitions. Preserve source designs, populations, times, comparisons, heterogeneity, counterevidence and the distinction between original authors' interpretation, synthesis and hypotheses. Do not impose IMRAD or replan the review.
